pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
This fixes #63936 and #63937

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request


##### COMPONENT NAME
lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/vmware_vm_inventory.py

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The verify file method was removed because it is already implemented by the auto plugin and the current one prevented the plugin from being used by auto plugin. 

Tower/AWX inject credentials using specific environment variables (https://github.com/ansible/awx/blob/602ee856fa03c7e0ab5d773cd04af2f2fad17022/awx/main/models/credential/injectors.py#L69). They are corrected here to match the ones injected to make the built in credential useful in Tower/AWX

issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
The vmware_vm_inventory plugin cannot verify the inventory file when being loaded via the auto plugin

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/vmware_vm_inventory.py

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```paste below
ansible 2.8.1
  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/Users/wtome/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/local/Cellar/ansible/2.8.1_1/libexec/lib/python3.7/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/local/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.7.4 (default, Sep  7 2019, 18:27:02) [Clang 10.0.1 (clang-1001.0.46.4)]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
```paste below

```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
MacOS 10.14.6


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
vmware_vm_inventory.yaml
```yaml
---
plugin: vmware_vm_inventory
strict: True
```

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
Inventory should be parsed from vCenter

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
```paste below
ansible-inventory -i vmware_vm_inventory.yaml --playbook-dir=. --list
 [WARNING]:  * Failed to parse /Users/wtome/ansible-
inventory/tests/vmware_vm_inventory.yaml with auto plugin: inventory config
'/Users/wtome/ansible-
inventory/tests/vmware_vm_inventory.yaml' could not be verified by plugin
'vmware_vm_inventory'
```

I just wanted to add a note in case anyone else stumbles upon this pre-2.10 and thinks that they cannot use `auto`: The file should end with `vmware.yaml` or `vmware.yml` and the file should contain `plugin: vmware_vm_inventory`. In 2.10 (thanks to this commit bbbaf0dfe775bb7ab8584244a7162cd3a9a5f9a5) your file name can also end with `vmware_vm_inventory.yaml` or `vmware_vm_inventory.yml`, but that enhancement is unrelated to making `auto` work.

Minor nit - if someone had both `VMWARE_SERVER`, and `VMWARE_HOST` set, VMWARE_SERVER was used. Now `VMWARE_HOST` has a higher precedence (last one wins). You could reorder to ensure compatibility:
```
            env:
              - name: VMWARE_HOST
              - name: VMWARE_SERVER
```
Probably unlikely to affect anyone, but perhaps worth mentioning.

AWX does not yet use this inventory plugin. When we do, obviously we will want to use the most future-proof parameters. For current vmware inventory imports we use the script, and its config follows this pattern:

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/contrib/inventory/vmware.ini

You can see we put the host/username/password in that config file

https://github.com/ansible/awx/blob/4a1c1217922570dc8361d33efd3b14d74529e645/awx/main/models/inventory.py#L2455

This will be going away entirely as the plugin replaces it.

However, this is how credentials are applied for _job_ (playbook) runs:

https://github.com/ansible/awx/blob/4a1c1217922570dc8361d33efd3b14d74529e645/awx/main/models/credential/injectors.py#L68-L72

That uses `VMWARE_HOST` that you mention.

AWX _can_ use different environment variables for inventory updates versus playbook runs. But why should we? Is it not reasonable to expect that inventory plugins accept credentials by the same environment variables as the modules?

So to answer what we _should_ do, we should look to the vmware modules for example.

https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/2.6/modules/vmware_guest_module.html#vmware-guest-module

> If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable VMWARE_HOST will be used instead.

This inventory script used VMWARE_HOST

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/contrib/inventory/vmware.py

But _this_ inventory script (the one used by AWX) uses VMWARE_SERVER

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/contrib/inventory/vmware_inventory.py

There might be a reason for this. Maybe they server different purposes, and the server vs. host refers to different things. But maybe not, I don't know.
